Correct. Van ’t Hoff: d(pKa)/dT = −ΔH°/(2.303 R T²); for an ammonium group ΔH° ≈ +45 kJ/mol, so pKa falls by about 0.026 per K, whereas carboxylic acids (ΔH° ≈ 0) barely change. So temperature does change ionization constants, in a group-dependent way; the statement that it has no effect is false.
